questions.q_en:
In the following question below consists of a question and two statements, I and II were given below it.

Seven boys in a class scored different marks in a math test. F scored higher than D. B scored more than at least two people. E scored second highest marks. C scored more than G but less than D. How many people scored more than B?

I. A scored more than F. B scored less than F.

II. D scored less than B. A scored more than C.

Read both the statements and mark your answer as:
options_en: If the data in statement I alone are sufficient to answer the question, while the data in statement II alone are not sufficient to answer the question
If the data in statement II alone are sufficient to answer the question, while the data in statement I alone are not sufficient to answer the question
If the data either in statement I alone or in statement II alone are sufficient to answer the question
If the data in both statements I and II together are necessary to answer the question
questions.solution_en:
F scored higher than D. B scored more than at least two people. E scored second highest marks. C scored more than G but less than D.

Considering statement I:

A scored more than F. B scored less than F.

So statement I alone is not sufficient.

Considering statement II:

D scored less than B. A scored more than C.

So, statement II alone is also not sufficient.

Combining both the statements we get:

So, three people scored more than B.

LHS is equal to RHS.

LHS is not equal to RHS.

questions.q_en: Five boys Aman, Baman, Chaman, Daman and Farhan have different ages. Farhan is elder than only Aman and Baman, Daman is younger than only Chaman, Aman is not the youngest. How many boys are elder than Aman?
questions.solution_en:
Farhan is elder than only Aman and Baman.

· Farhan > Aman/Baman > Baman/Aman

Daman is younger than only Chaman.

· Chaman > Daman > Farhan > Aman/Baman > Baman/Aman

Aman is not the youngest.

· Chaman > Daman > Farhan > Aman > Baman

Hence, three people Chaman, Daman, and Farhan are elder than Aman.
questions.solution_hi:
Farhan is elder than only Aman and Baman.

· Farhan > Aman/Baman > Baman/Aman

Daman is younger than only Chaman.

· Chaman > Daman > Farhan > Aman/Baman > Baman/Aman

Aman is not the youngest.

· Chaman > Daman > Farhan > Aman > Baman

Hence, three people Chaman, Daman, and Farhan are elder than Aman.

questions.q_en: Find the number of triangles in the figure given below -
questions.solution_en:
Consider one square

AEB, AEC, ABC, BED, DEC, BCD, ABD and ACD are all possible triangles.

So, no. of triangles in one square = 8

So, by symmetry all 4 squares will have 8 triangles each

Thus, no. of triangles in all squares together considering one square at a time = 4*8 = 32

Now, consider all squares combined together

PQR, STU, RVW, ZST, QRV and TUY are all possible triangles

So, no. of triangles considering all squares combined together = 6

So, the total no. of triangles formed = 32 + 6 = 38
